chunks: And Abān narrated from al-Ḥakam, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:
“If a child is taken for hajj, then he has fulfilled the hajj of Islam only until he grows up; and if a servant is taken for hajj, then he has fulfilled the hajj of Islam only until he is freed.”

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: a child who has not yet reached legal maturity
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required in Islam
key_terms.يَكْبَرَ: to reach maturity or grow up

ai.seo_question: Does a hajj performed in childhood or slavery count as the obligatory Hajj of Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a hajj performed by a child or a slave is not sufficient for the obligatory hajj required after legal responsibility or freedom is attained. It establishes a fiqh ruling concerning the validity and discharge of hajj obligations in different legal states.
